svg.text: HIL interface — what the HIL simulates, what crosses the boundary, what is real (IDCFC, Delta Cup 2026 final)

Plant = MODEL.md v0.4.4, one 800 VDC distribution segment at full scale (132 kW); two real STM32H743 sensing nodes decide on the HIL's analog outputs and open the model's breakers. Thai summary in the brief.

Numerics the box must support: explicit fixed-step integration (RK4 or Euler) of 11 states — implicit solvers break the controller's anti-windup rule (MODEL.md §4.8);
healthy-network time constants ≥ 10 µs and 5 kHz resonance; the fault branch (τ_f down to 0.05 µs) is integrated quasi-statically when the step exceeds 0.5·τ_f (MODEL.md 0.4.4 rule, validated);

every discontinuity (load step, fault on/off, UVLO, breaker) lands on a step boundary. Step ≤ 1 µs is comfortable; ≤ 10 µs is being evaluated by our front-end sweep. Reference: Python core + Simscape check (i), 8/8 cases ≤ 1 %.
Model forms we can supply: (a) Simscape Electrical .slx (simscape/dcsim_shelf.slx, the validated cross-check model; variable-step network + discrete controller);

(b) pure Simulink fixed-step explicit ODE model (MATLAB Function RK4 of the 11 states — being prepared, validated against the same 8 cases); (c) the equations (MODEL.md) and the Python reference, if the box has its own solver / FPGA netlist.
DO1 SYNC (the only SYNC source in HIL mode)
16-bit DAC at 5 MS/s is ample (the nodes sample at 500 kSa/s behind a 100 kHz filter)
Open: solver step, model import path, DI/DO levels (level shift on the adapter panel), DI sampling rate, PC link. Layer 1 off by default (on only for a bolted-fault demo).

Meeting demo (≈ 15 min): 1 the HTML explainer (what the relay does, 3 min) · 2 open dcsim_shelf.slx, run one case live (step, ~1 min) and show the Python-vs-Simscape overlay for all eight cases (Figure 5) ·

3 this diagram: what the box simulates, the four outputs, the three inputs, scaling · 4 the fixed-step explicit version running at the step the box supports, scored by the same check (i) · 5 questions: solver step, import path, DI/DO levels, PC link, venue.

What the HIL proves to the judges: the relay protecting the full-scale 800 V design in closed loop with trip time measured by lab equipment; the 120 W bench proves the same firmware on real sensors and real faults.
